scope: School mock Physics 7408 AS Electricity 3.5 and Chemistry 7405 AS Group 2 3.2.2, Group 7 3.2.3 and identification practical observations. No year-2 Maths, buffers or untaught Chemistry.
reviewMethod: Conservative: reuse individually saved prior evidence (front/back where available) with topic-specific AQA text. New original applied problems test harder combined reasoning; no retrospective claim that this is all spec bullets.

items.requirement: Electric current means charge flowing per unit time
items.front: What is electric current?
items.back: I = ΔQ/Δt, rate of flow of charge.

items.requirement: Potential difference means energy transferred per unit charge
items.front: Define potential difference.
items.back: Energy transferred per unit charge: V = W/Q.

items.requirement: Resistance is potential difference divided by current
items.front: What is resistance?
items.back: R = V/I.

items.requirement: Ohm's law requires constant physical conditions
items.front: What condition is required for Ohm's law?
items.back: Constant physical conditions, including temperature.

items.requirement: Interpret why a filament lamp is non-ohmic
items.front: Why does a filament lamp's resistance rise at high current?
items.back: The filament gets hotter, increasing lattice vibrations and electron collisions.

items.requirement: Explain diode current–voltage characteristics
items.front: How does an idealised diode conduct?
items.back: It conducts strongly in the forward direction after its threshold and very little in reverse.

items.requirement: Distinguish gradients of I against V and V against I
items.front: For an ohmic conductor, what is the gradient of V against I versus I against V?
items.back: V (y) vs I (x): gradient = R. I (y) vs V (x): gradient = 1/R.

items.requirement: An ideal ammeter has zero resistance
items.front: What is an ideal ammeter's resistance?
items.back: Zero.

items.requirement: An ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance
items.front: What is an ideal voltmeter's resistance?
items.back: Infinite.

items.requirement: Use relationship between resistivity, R, L and A
items.front: What equation links resistance and resistivity?
items.back: R = ρL/A.

items.requirement: Recall resistivity unit
items.front: What is the unit of resistivity in base units?
items.back: Ω m.

items.requirement: Explain metal resistance increasing with temperature
items.front: Why does a metal's resistance often rise with temperature?
items.back: Greater lattice vibrations increase electron scattering.

items.requirement: NTC thermistor resistance falls when temperature increases
items.front: For an NTC thermistor, what happens to resistance as temperature rises?
items.back: Resistance decreases.

items.requirement: Superconductors have zero resistivity below a critical temperature
items.front: What is a superconductor?
items.back: A material with zero resistivity below its critical temperature.

items.requirement: Recognise one application of a superconductor
items.front: Name one use of superconductors in the AQA specification.
items.back: Strong magnetic fields or lower energy losses in power transmission.

items.requirement: Use resistance–length graph gradient in practical 5
items.front: What does the gradient of resistance against wire length give?
items.back: ρ/A, for a wire of constant cross-section.

items.requirement: Series components carry equal current
items.front: What is true of current in a series circuit?
items.back: The current is the same at every point.

items.requirement: Series potential differences add to supply p.d.
items.front: What happens to p.d. in a series circuit?
items.back: The supply p.d. equals the sum of component p.d.s.

items.requirement: Parallel branches have equal p.d.
items.front: What is true of p.d. across parallel branches?
items.back: It is the same across each branch.

items.requirement: Current entering and leaving a circuit junction is equal
items.front: How does current behave at a junction?
items.back: Total current into a junction equals total current out.

items.requirement: Recall electrical power formulae
items.front: Give three electrical power equations.
items.back: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.

items.requirement: Equivalent resistance in series is sum of resistances
items.front: How do the resistances of series-connected components combine?
items.back: Rₜ = R₁ + R₂ + … .

items.requirement: Equivalent resistance in parallel uses reciprocals
items.front: What is the rule for equivalent resistance of two parallel resistors?
items.back: 1/Rₜ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

items.requirement: Combine identical cells in series accounting for internal resistance
items.front: For n identical cells connected in series, what are the total emf and internal resistance?
items.back: Total emf = nε; total internal resistance = nr.

items.requirement: Combine identical cells in parallel accounting for internal resistance
items.front: For n identical cells connected in parallel, what are the total emf and internal resistance?
items.back: Total emf = ε; total internal resistance = r/n.

items.requirement: Unloaded divider output depends on resistance fraction
items.front: For two series resistors, how is output p.d. found?
items.back: Vout = Vin × R₂/(R₁ + R₂), taking R₂ across the output.

items.requirement: Loading the lower divider resistor reduces effective resistance
items.front: Why can loading the lower part of a divider lower its output voltage?
items.back: The parallel load lowers that branch resistance and its share of the supply p.d.

items.requirement: NTC thermistor in lower divider branch reduces output on heating
items.front: What happens to Vout across an NTC thermistor as temperature increases?
items.back: Vout falls when supply voltage and the other series resistance are fixed.

items.requirement: Emf is energy supplied per unit charge
items.front: Define emf.
items.back: Energy supplied by the source per unit charge.

items.requirement: Terminal voltage is emf minus internal-resistance lost volts
items.front: A cell has emf ε, internal resistance r and current I. What is its terminal p.d.?
items.back: V = ε − Ir. The term Ir is the lost volts inside the cell.

items.requirement: On graph of terminal p.d. V against current I, intercept gives emf, gradient -r
items.front: For a graph of terminal p.d. V against current I, what are the intercept and gradient?
items.back: y-intercept = emf ε and gradient = −r.

items.requirement: A cell with no current has terminal p.d. equal to emf
items.front: What is the terminal p.d. of a cell when no current flows?
items.back: It equals the emf because the lost volts Ir are zero.

items.requirement: Required practical 6 uses graph terminal p.d. against current
items.front: Which graph is used to find a cell's emf and internal resistance?
items.back: Terminal p.d. V against current I.

legacyTestCards.front: What precipitate colours identify chloride, bromide and iodide after acidifying and adding AgNO₃?
legacyTestCards.back: AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow.

legacyTestCards.front: How does Group 2 metal reactivity change down the group?
How does Group 2 hydroxide solubility change down the group?
How does Group 2 sulfate solubility change down the group?
How does halide-ion reducing power change down Group 7?
When will one halogen displace another halide?
legacyTestCards.back: A more reactive/stronger oxidising halogen displaces the halide of a less reactive halogen.

legacyTestCards.front: Why is chlorine a stronger oxidising agent than iodine?
legacyTestCards.back: Chlorine attracts and gains electrons more readily due to smaller size and less shielding.

mathsScope: AS Year 1 Pure first mock; Year 2, Mechanics, Statistics excluded; no changes to Maths data
limits: This is an answer-evidence audit of the named 33 Physics requirements and selected Chemistry tests, not all AQA requirements.
The 57 marks are from original questions; no official paper provenance or historical full-paper coverage is claimed.
Chemical content is conceptual interpretation of hypothetical observations, not laboratory method instructions.
Student mastery, performance of practicals, full automated ECF and reliable diagram recognition not certified.
Unchanged base deck, exam bank, cloud-progress IDs, XP, scanner, World media.
